newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-FTSE options heavily traded as shares dive.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-FTSE options heavily traded as shares dive.

text.p: Activity in UK equity options on Wednesday was concentrated in the FTSE 100 index owing to a combination of June contracts expiring at the end of the week and an early sell-off in the stock market, dealers said.

This powerful cocktail of high volatility and near-term expiry can produce huge profits or losses and cause frantic scenes on the trading floor as traders vie for the best prices -- either to open new positions or to close existing ones.
The June 4600 puts, which expire on Friday, were the most active series in FTSE due to mixed trading.
One large deal was a buy 4,500 June 4600 puts for a few pence, with the dealer betting on a further sharp fall in the cash market.
Another trader sold 2,000 lots in the same series, possibly in a closing deal.

Some traders preferred to sell call options hoping to make money by capturing options premium as the market falls away. In this category, one large deal was to sell 800 July 4650 calls at prices between 107p to 113p while in another bargain, 800 July 4625 calls were sold at 108p.
By 1300 GMT, cash FTSE was down 43.1 points to 4,639.1 while June FTSE futures were down 41 at 4,640.
Over in stock options, satellite television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting was active ahead of the contract's 1700 GMT expiry.

The main deal was a buy of 1,000 June 550 puts at 18p. BSkyB shares dropped 39-1/2p to 527p on fears the company may be forced to leave a consortium that is bidding for a new digital television licences.
Elsewhere, a short put position was rolled forward in conglomerate Lonrho when a trader bought back 700 June 140 puts at 10p and sold 700 September 140 puts at 13p.
